land.text: the Byzantine cities of Nicaea and briefly Nicomedia, gained 1075-1081

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Byzantine Empire, Seljuk Empire, Danishmends, Mengujekids, Saltukids, Artuqids'; the Danishmends, Mengujekids and Saltukids were absorbed later and appear as counterparts of gain events.

land.text: the plateau around Iconium and Ankara that Rum held after 1097; the page does not locate the Seljuk-held land at the secession

predecessors.note: 'seceded from the Seljuk Empire under Suleiman ibn Qutalmish in 1077'; Malik-Shah recognised it as a vassal in 1084 (infobox: Seljuk vassal 1078-1092).

land.text: Konya and the plateau; the infobox gives 'Karamanid conquest: 1308', and the Karamanids conquered a relative's lands, a brief holder of Konya, in 1328

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Anatolian beyliks and the Ilkhanate'; the other beyliks of 1305-1313 (Hamid, Germiyan, Eshrefids, Kastamonu, Ahi) took western and northern parts.

land.text: Anatolia under Ilkhanid administration: 'Seljuk power declined until the dynasty died out in 1308, and its territories passed to the Ilkhanate' (Köse Dağ page)

successors.note: The Ilkhanids were the suzerains from 1256.

capitals.name: Nicaea (İznik)
capitals.note: Infobox: Nicaea 1077-1097; surrendered to the Byzantines on 19 June 1097.

capitals.name: Iconium (Konya)
capitals.note: Infobox: Iconium 1097-1308; the Byzantine-Seljuk wars page has it the capital 'around 1101'.

capitals.name: Sebastia (Sivas)
capitals.note: Infobox: Sebastia 1211-1220, listed beside Konya; the Kaykaus I page does not call Sivas a capital.

capitals.name: Caesarea (Kayseri)
capitals.note: 'In 1303 Mesud II established himself as sultan in Kayseri.'

rulers.name: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish
rulers.note: Table: 1075-1077 de facto, 1077-1086 recognised by Malik-Shah I; died at Ain Salm in 1086. Clamped to the state start (1077) by reviewer me-09-b.

rulers.name: Kilij Arslan I
rulers.note: Died fighting Mehmed Tapar after capturing Mosul in 1107.

rulers.name: Kaykhusraw I
rulers.note: First reign; lost a civil war to his brother Suleiman II in 1196.

rulers.name: Kaykhusraw I
rulers.note: Second reign; killed at Antioch on the Meander in 1211.

rulers.name: Kaykaus II
rulers.note: Table 1246-1262; the text has him in the west to 1260, when he fled to Crimea.

rulers.name: Kilij Arslan IV
rulers.note: Co-ruler in the east under Mongol administration; the text gives 1248-1265; executed 1265.

rulers.name: Kaykhusraw III
rulers.note: 'the nominal ruler of all of Anatolia'; executed 1284.

rulers.name: Mesud II
rulers.note: Second reign, from Kayseri; murdered in 1308.

correction.text: Nicaea and its district, with Nicomedia briefly: Suleiman 'gained control of the Byzantine cities of Nicaea' (1075-1081); no extent is given for 1086-1092, when Suleiman was dead and Kilij Arslan I a captive

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Rum shape begins in 1094 but the sultanate was founded in 1077 (infobox 'seceded from the Seljuk Empire under Suleiman ibn Qutalmish in 1077'). The core is the page's Nicaea; the extent in 1086-1093 is bridged at confidence 1.

correction.text: the 1094 shape, valid 1094-1096 only: after the First Crusade Nicaea went back to the Byzantines on 19 June 1097 and John Doukas took the western cities

keyframe_review.note: 367,020 km2, bbox west to 25.8 E: Nicaea, Smyrna, Dorylaeum and Afyon are inside; the infobox gives no area. 'Kilij Arslan withdrew' from Nicaea, which 'surrendered to the Byzantines on 19 June' 1097, and John Doukas took 'the cities of Smyrna, Ephesus, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea and Choma'. Antalya and Kastamonu are inside the shape; no page says Rum held them in 1094 (unverified).

correction.text: what remained after the First Crusade and the Byzantine recovery: the plateau around Iconium (Konya), Ankara and Aksaray

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria keeps the 1094 shape to 1098 although Nicaea fell in June 1097 and the western cities in 1097; the 1099 shape is used two years early. The crusaders also took Sozopolis, Philomelium, Iconium, Antioch in Pisidia, Heraclea and Caesarea in 1097, but 'Caesarea returned to the Seljuks' and Iconium became the capital.

1099-1138, 128,919 km2: the plateau around Konya, Ankara and Aksaray. The infobox gives no area to compare; 'Upon Mesud's death in 1156, the sultanate controlled nearly all of central Anatolia'. John II's 1130s gains (Kastamonu, Gangra and the southern coast; the page does not date them) lie outside this shape.
1139-1146, 128,756 km2, unchanged. Manuel I 'launched a campaign against Konya' in 1146; the page gives no result and no land changed.
1147-1151, 129,149 km2, unchanged through the Second Crusade (1147-1150), which touched Rum's neighbours, not its land.

correction.text: the 1152 shape, valid 1152-1173 only: 'when Nur ad-Din died in 1174, the Sivas lands were incorporated into the Sultanate'

keyframe_review.note: 1152-1176, 129,169 km2. Kilij Arslan II attacked the Danishmend Yaghibasan in 1155 but the Sivas lands were incorporated only in 1174 (Danishmends page); the Myriokephalon page agrees ('After the death of Nureddin Zangi in 1174, the Sultan conquered the Danishmend emirates'). The 1177 shape is therefore used three years early (next keyframe). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1152..1173 from this entry's own 'valid 1152-1173 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the Danishmend lands around Sivas incorporated in 1174, drawn as Cliopatria's 1177 shape; Malatya still Danishmend until 1178

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1174-1176, the 1177 shape three years earlier. Fahreddin died in 1172 and by 1175 Nasreddin Muhammed was back as a Seljuk vassal (Danishmends page); the page's only explicit absorption is 1174.
1177-1187, 173,237 km2, bbox east to 38.9 E. 'In 1178, Malatya was occupied. This event marked the end of the Danishmend rule'; Cliopatria adds Malatya only in 1192. 1177 itself stands as drawn.

correction.text: the 1188 shape plus Malatya (it is missing from Cliopatria's 1188-1191 shape), valid 1188-1191

keyframe_review.note: 1188-1191, 252,369 km2: the shape adds Kayseri and the west to Dorylaeum and Afyon. No page opened dates these western and Kayseri gains (the Byzantine-Seljuk wars page: 'After 1180 Turkish pressure moved further west' with no 1180s detail), so they stay at confidence 1: unverified, page budget. Kilij Arslan II divided the sultanate among his sons from 1186-1192.

1192-1201, 258,075 km2, bbox east to 39.8 E. 'Following Kilij Arslan II's death, the sultanate was divided amongst his sons'; Tughril received Elbistan, and Erzurum was taken from the Saltukids only 'at the start of the 13th century' (Rum page), as Cliopatria draws it from 1202. Reviewer me-09-b: the earlier adjust adding Erzurum from 1192 was withdrawn.

1202-1205, 319,379 km2. Antalya is inside the shape but Kaykhusraw I 'seized Antalya in 1207' (Kaykhusraw I page; Rum page 'Kaykhusraw I captured Attalia ... in 1207'). The jump to 27.6 E in the west and 41.6 E at Erzurum is otherwise unexplained by any page opened (Kastamonu, Kayseri, Afyon stay: unverified, page budget). The Rum page reports Suleiman II's defeat by Georgia at Basiani in 1203 or 1204 and his withdrawal to Erzurum.

correction.text: the 1206 shape without Antalya for 1206 only; from 1207 the shape stands as drawn

keyframe_review.note: 1206-1209, 329,286 km2: 'Kaykhusraw I captured Attalia (Antalya), on the Mediterranean coast in 1207', one year after the shape adds it.

minus.text: Erzurum, 'broke free from the Seljuk state'

correction.text: the 1210 shape without Erzurum, valid 1212-1213; 1210-1211 as drawn

keyframe_review.note: 1210-1215, 347,252 km2. 'In 1211-1212 Tughril broke free from the Seljuk state', so Erzurum leaves the sultanate; the shape's northern reach to 41.98 N is short of Sinop, which came in 1214 (next keyframe).

correction.text: the 1210 shape without Erzurum plus Sinop, which Alexios of Trebizond handed over after his capture in 1214

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Kaykaus I 'captured Sinop and made the Empire of Trebizond his vassal in 1214' (Rum page); in exchange for his freedom Alexios 'handed over Sinop, a Black Sea port, and accepted the vassalage of Trapezuntine territory'. Cliopatria's Sinop-reaching 1216 shape begins two years later.

minus.text: Erzurum held by Tughril and then Jahan Shah until 1230

keyframe_review.note: 1216-1226, 347,467 km2, the sultanate near its peak with Sinop; Erzurum is still outside until 'Jahan Shah lost the Battle of Yassıçemen' in 1230. Aleppo was only briefly in play: 'forced to surrender Aleppo' (1218). The infobox gives no peak area to compare.

correction.text: the 1216 shape without Erzurum plus Alanya, taken by Kayqubad I in 1221 from its governor Kir Fard, and the Mediterranean coast taken 1221-1225

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Kayqubad I 'took the port of Kalon Oros, later renamed Ala'iyya' in 1221; Cliopatria's 1216-1249 shapes stop short of the Alanya coast. The Cilician Armenia plain stays outside; its king became a vassal in 1225.

correction.text: the 1227 shape plus Alanya and the Ahlat and Lake Van region, valid 1230-1233 (Erzurum returns with Yassıçemen; 1227-1229 is the previous keyframe)

keyframe_review.note: 1227-1249, 347,276 km2. After Yassıçimen (1230) Kayqubad 'established Seljuq rule over Erzurum, Ahlat, and the Lake Van region, which had been Ayyubid territory'. Cliopatria shows Erzurum from 1202 and never the Lake Van basin.

correction.text: the 1227 shape plus Alanya, Lake Van, and from 1234 Siverek, Urfa, Harran and Raqqa and from 1237 the Diyarbakır region

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1234 Kayqubad completely defeated the allied Ayyubid forces. He then took Siverek, Urfa, Harran, and Raqqa'; 'Kaykhusraw II began by capturing the region around Diyarbakır' (1237, Rum page). The pages do not say how long these Ayyubid lands stayed in Rum; the Mongols took Erzurum in 1242 and, after Köse Dağ (1243), Kayseri, Sivas, Erzincan and Ankara (Köse Dağ page), yet the sultanate stayed a client kingdom, so the shape is kept to 1249 as Cliopatria has it. Raqqa and Urfa are very likely raids: confidence 2.

1250-1259, 192,085 km2, bbox east to 35.95 E: the west under Kaykaus II. 'Kaykaus II held the west; Kilij Arslan IV and Kayqubad II ruled the east under Mongol administration' (1249-1260/62). In October 1256 Bayju defeated Kaykaus II near Aksaray and 'all of Anatolia became officially subject to Möngke Khan'. The infobox gives no area. Cilician Armenia 'took the Mediterranean coast from the Seljuk in the 1240s' (Rum page), which this shape already excludes.

correction.text: the nominal sultanate under Ilkhanid administration, drawn as the core Cliopatria shows in 1305 (Kayseri-Aksaray); Kaykaus II fled to Crimea in 1260 and Kaykhusraw III was 'the nominal ruler of all of Anatolia' from 1265 to 1284

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Rum shape for 1260-1304, but the Rum page keeps the sultanate alive as 'Ilkhanid vassal (1256-1308)' under Kilij Arslan IV (to 1266), Kaykhusraw III (1266-1284), Mesud II, Kayqubad III. The extent is a bridge at confidence 1: no page opened gives it; the Mongol Empire and Ilkhanate shapes cover the land in this period. The Karamanids captured Konya briefly in 1277.

correction.text: the 1305 shape, valid 1305-1308 only: Mesud II was murdered in 1308 and the Karamanids conquered the sultanate

keyframe_review.note: 1305-1313, 71,760 km2 around Kayseri and Aksaray: 'In 1303 Mesud II established himself as sultan in Kayseri'; 'He was murdered in 1308 and his son Mesud III soon afterwards'; infobox 'Karamanid conquest: 1308'. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1313; 1309-1313 belongs to the Karamanids, Ilkhanate and other beyliks. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1305..1308 from this entry's own 'valid 1305-1308 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: Nicaea, the capital, and the cities Suleiman won from the Byzantines in 1075-1081

ledger.note: 1077: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish founds the Sultanate of Rum at Nicaea. It 'seceded from the Seljuk Empire under Suleiman ibn Qutalmish in 1077'; 1075-1081 he 'gained control of the Byzantine cities of Nicaea' and briefly Nicomedia; Malik-Shah recognised it only as a subordinate state in 1084. The page gives the cities, not a boundary.

region.text: Smyrna, Ephesus, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea and Choma

ledger.note: 1097: the Byzantines retake the western cities. A Byzantine campaign in 1097 led by John Doukas took 'the cities of Smyrna, Ephesus, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea and Choma from the demoralised Turks'. Cliopatria draws the loss in 1099.
1097: the capital moves from Nicaea to Iconium (Konya) (infobox 'Iconium (Konya), 1097-1308'); the Byzantine-Seljuk wars page has Iconium the capital 'around 1101'.

region.text: Nicaea

ledger.note: 19 June 1097: Nicaea surrenders to the Byzantines. The crusaders besieged it from 6 May 1097; 'Kilij Arslan withdrew' and the city 'surrendered to the Byzantines on 19 June'.

region.text: the Sivas lands of the Danishmends

ledger.note: 1174: Sivas absorbed. 'when Nur ad-Din died in 1174, the Sivas lands were incorporated into the Sultanate'; Kilij Arslan II had attacked Yaghibasan in 1155.

region.text: Malatya, the end of Danishmend rule

ledger.note: 1178: Malatya occupied. 'In 1178, Malatya was occupied. This event marked the end of the Danishmend rule, while the remaining Danishmends joined Seljuk service.'

region.text: the strip Cliopatria adds in 1188: Kayseri and the west to Dorylaeum and Afyon

ledger.note: Page silent: no page opened dates these gains. The Byzantine-Seljuk wars page says only that after the Turkish raids to the Aegean (1177-1180) 'Turkish pressure moved further west into Byzantine territory'. A gap-filler should open 'Kilij Arslan II' and the Danishmend page on Kayseri (Caesarea).

region.text: Konya

ledger.note: 1190: Holy Roman Empire forces reach Konya during the Third Crusade. The page records 'a temporary occupation of Konya in 1190' by Holy Roman Empire forces; it names no month.

region.text: Konya

ledger.note: 1190: the crusaders leave Konya; the page calls the occupation temporary.

region.text: Erzurum, 'taken from the Saltukids at the start of the 13th century', where Tughril was installed

ledger.note: 1202 (reviewer me-09-b, was 1192): Erzurum is taken from the Saltukids. The Rum page: 'Elbistan was given to Tughril ibn Kılıç Arslan II, but when Erzurum was taken from the Saltukids' at the start of the 13th century he was installed there; it also says 'Tughril governed Erzurum from 1192 to 1221', but in 1192 he received Elbistan. The year 1202 is Cliopatria's, matching 'the start of the 13th century'.

region.text: Antalya (Attalia), the Mediterranean port

ledger.note: 1207: Kaykhusraw I takes Antalya. He 'seized Antalya in 1207 from its Niceaen garrison', giving the sultanate a Mediterranean port; the Rum page: 'captured Attalia (Antalya), on the Mediterranean coast in 1207'.
1211: the court moves to Sivas (infobox 'Sebastia (Sivas), 1211-1220'); the Kaykaus I page does not call Sivas a capital.

region.text: Erzurum, from which Tughril 'broke free from the Seljuk state'

ledger.note: 1211-1212: Tughril of Erzurum secedes. 'Tughril broke free from the Seljuk state' in 1211-1212 (the span is the page's); he governed Erzurum to 1221, followed by Jahan Shah.

region.text: the Trapezuntine territory east of Sinop

ledger.note: 1214: Trebizond becomes a Rum vassal. Kaykaus 'made the Empire of Trebizond his vassal in 1214'; after a revolt Kayqubad I besieged it in 1222-1223 and 'forced the Komnenos dynasty family to renew their pledges of vassalage' (Kayqubad I page).

region.text: Sinop, the Black Sea port

ledger.note: 1214: Kaykaus I takes Sinop. Turkmen tribesmen captured Alexios, Grand Komnenos of Trebizond, in 1214 and 'in exchange for his freedom, Alexios handed over Sinop'; the page gives the transfer as 'Sunday 1 November', year from the Rum page ('captured Sinop ... in 1214').
1221: Konya is again the only capital (infobox Sivas 1211-1220).

region.text: Alanya (Kalon Oros)

ledger.note: 1221: Kayqubad I takes Alanya. He took the port of Kalon Oros, later Ala'iyya, 'from its governor, Kir Fard', who surrendered peacefully; the Rum page adds that he 'continued to acquire lands along the Mediterranean coast' in 1221-1225.

region.text: the Cilician plain and its kingdom

ledger.note: 1225: Cilician Armenia becomes a Rum vassal. Kayqubad 'reduced the kingdom of Cilician Armenia to a vassal state' (the page puts the Cilicia campaign in 1225); the Kaykaus I page has Kaykaus subjugating the Armenians earlier, undated and marked 'citation needed'.

region.text: Erzurum, annexed after Yassıçemen

ledger.counterpart: Jahan Shah of Erzurum (Seljuk cadet branch)
ledger.note: 1230: Erzurum annexed. 'Jahan Shah lost the Battle of Yassıçemen, allowing for Erzurum to be annexed by the Seljuk sultanate.'

region.text: Ahlat and the Lake Van region

ledger.note: 1230: Kayqubad finally defeats Jalal al-Din at Yassıçimen 'between Sivas and Erzincan in 1230' and establishes Seljuq rule over 'Erzurum, Ahlat, and the Lake Van region, which had been Ayyubid territory'. The page gives no separate date for Ahlat.

region.text: Siverek, Urfa, Harran and Raqqa

ledger.note: 1234: Kayqubad defeats the Ayyubids. 'In 1234 Kayqubad completely defeated the allied Ayyubid forces. He then took Siverek, Urfa, Harran, and Raqqa.' The page does not say how long they were held (probably raids: confidence 2); 'The Ayyubids of Syria later recognized his sovereignty.'

region.text: the region around Diyarbakır

ledger.note: 1237: Kaykhusraw II takes the Diyarbakır region. 'Kaykhusraw II began by capturing the region around Diyarbakır' (reign 1237-1246); the page does not say from whom.

region.text: Erzurum, besieged for about two months and sacked

ledger.note: 1242: the Mongols take Erzurum. 'In 1242, Baiju's army demanded Erzurum's submission'; after the envoys were rejected it was besieged for about two months, then sacked (Rum page: 'The forces of the Mongol Empire took Erzurum in 1242').

region.text: Kayseri, Sivas, Erzincan and Ankara

ledger.note: 1243: Baiju invades Rum again. 'Baiju wintered on the Mughan plain and invaded Rum again in 1243'; Rum's forces assembled at Sivas. Köse Dağ lies about 80 km north-west of Sivas.

region.text: Kayseri, Sivas, Erzincan and Ankara

ledger.note: 26 June 1243: the Mongols crush Kaykhusraw II at Köse Dağ and then capture Kayseri, Sivas, Erzincan and Ankara; Rum 'was reduced to the status of a client kingdom' and the sultans swore allegiance. Rum stays one state as a Mongol vassal (infobox 1243-1256), so the vassal tint belongs to the Mongol dossier.

region.text: Trebizond, whose ruler Manuel I 'submitted to the Mongols'

ledger.note: 1243: Trebizond leaves Rum's overlordship. The page says its ruler submitted to the Mongols and 'likely attended Güyük's coronation in 1246'; no page dates the end of Rum's suzerainty, so 1243 is a bridge.

region.text: Cilician Armenia, which 'voluntarily submitted' to the Mongols

ledger.note: 1244: Cilicia submits to the Mongols and leaves Rum's overlordship. 'Cilician Armenia voluntarily submitted in 1244 and received lands and fortresses as a reward.'

region.text: the east half of the sultanate, from Kayseri to Erzurum and Lake Van

ledger.note: 1250: the east passes under Mongol administration. From 1249 'Kilij Arslan IV and Kayqubad II ruled the east under Mongol administration' while Kaykaus II held the west; Cliopatria draws the east out of the sultanate from 1250.

region.text: near Aksaray

ledger.note: October 1256: Bayju defeats Kaykaus II near Aksaray. 'In October 1256, Bayju defeated Kaykaus II near Aksaray and all of Anatolia became officially subject to Möngke Khan' (the table has 14 October at Sultanhanı).

region.text: near Aksaray

ledger.note: October 1256: Rum becomes an Ilkhanid vassal (infobox 1256-1308); Kaykaus II kept the west until he fled to Crimea in 1260.

region.text: the west of the 1250 shape, outside the Kayseri-Aksaray core that Cliopatria shows in 1305

ledger.note: Page silent on the extent: in 1260 Kaykaus II fled to Crimea and the west ceased to have a sultan of its own; Cliopatria has no Rum shape for 1260-1304 and covers the land with the Mongol Empire (and then the Ilkhanate). The dated event is the page's, the region is a bridge.

region.text: Konya

ledger.note: 1277: the Karamanids take Konya. After Baibars's victory over the Mongols at Elbistan, 'the Karamanids under Shams al-Din Mehmed managed to capture Konya, briefly installing Jimri as a puppet ruler'.

region.text: Konya

ledger.note: 1277: the Karamanid hold on Konya is brief ('briefly installing Jimri as a puppet ruler'); the page does not say who retook it or when.
1303: the court is at Kayseri. 'In 1303 Mesud II established himself as sultan in Kayseri' after internal struggles that followed Kaykhusraw III's execution in 1284.

region.text: the last sultanate around Kayseri and Aksaray

ledger.note: 1308: the last sultan is murdered and the Seljuks of Rum end. 'He was murdered in 1308 and his son Mesud III soon afterwards'; infobox 'Karamanid conquest: 1308'; 'Seljuk power declined until the dynasty died out in 1308, and its territories passed to the Ilkhanate' (Köse Dağ page).

wars.name: First Crusade (Anatolian campaign)

union.text: Smyrna, Ephesus, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea and Choma

zones.text: Nicaea and the western cities retaken by the Byzantines

wars.outcome: Kilij Arslan I defeated the People's Crusade in 1096 but was beaten by the princely armies and driven back into south-central Anatolia; Nicaea surrendered to the Byzantines on 19 June 1097 and John Doukas retook the western cities.
wars.note: The Rum page: 'victorious against the People's Crusade' in 1096, later 'defeated by princely soldiers of the First Crusade and driven back into south-central Anatolia'; the crusade of 1101 was won by Kilij Arslan I ('defeated three Crusade contingents').

wars.name: Byzantine campaigns against Konya
wars.outcome: Manuel I campaigned against Konya in 1146 (no result given) and was attacked near Kotyaeion on his return from Antioch in 1159 after Kilij Arslan II refused passage; no border moved.

wars.name: Danishmend conquest by Kilij Arslan II
wars.outcome: Kilij Arslan II attacked Yaghibasan in 1155, absorbed the Sivas lands when Nur ad-Din died in 1174 and occupied Malatya in 1178, ending Danishmend rule.

wars.name: Battle of Myriokephalon

zones.text: Dorylaeum and Sublaeum, the Byzantine forts to be demolished

wars.outcome: Seljuk victory on 17 September 1176; Manuel I demolished the fort at Sublaeum but left Dorylaeum, and Turks raided the Meander valley in 1177. 'The bulk of Byzantine Asia Minor was retained for more than a century after the battle.'
wars.note: The peace of 1161 broke down in 1175 when Kilij Arslan refused to hand over the Danishmend territory he had taken.

wars.name: Third Crusade at Konya
wars.outcome: Forces of the Holy Roman Empire made 'a temporary occupation of Konya in 1190'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Rum-Georgia war and Battle of Basiani
wars.outcome: Suleiman II was defeated by Georgia under Tamar and withdrew to Erzurum; the page gives 1203 or 1204 and no land change.

wars.name: Rum-Nicaea war and Battle of Antioch on the Meander

zones.text: Antalya, which 'Kaykhusraw seized ... in 1207 from its Niceaen garrison'
Antioch on the Meander, where 'Kaykhusraw was killed at the Battle of Antioch on the Meander in 1211'

wars.outcome: Kaykhusraw I seized Antalya from its Nicaean garrison in 1207 and was killed at Antioch on the Meander in 1211; Kaykaus I then made a treaty with Theodore Laskaris.
wars.note: Manuel Maurozomes held Chonae and Laodicea as a vassal of Kaykhusraw; no date is given.

wars.name: Siege of Sinope
wars.outcome: Alexios of Trebizond, captured by Turkmen, handed Sinop over and accepted vassalage; the walls were rebuilt April-September 1215.

wars.name: Kayqubad I's coastal and Cilician campaigns
wars.outcome: Alanya taken in 1221; Trebizond besieged in 1222-1223 and forced to renew vassalage; Cilician Armenia reduced to a vassal state in 1225.

wars.name: Battle of Yassıçemen and the Khwarazmian war
wars.outcome: Jalal al-Din took Ahlat; Kayqubad defeated him at Yassıçimen in 1230 and annexed Erzurum, Ahlat and the Lake Van region.

wars.name: Rum-Ayyubid war of 1234
wars.outcome: Kayqubad 'completely defeated the allied Ayyubid forces' in 1234 and took Siverek, Urfa, Harran and Raqqa.
wars.note: Start year 1233 is a bridge; the page gives only 1234.

wars.name: Battle of Köse Dağ

zones.text: Erzurum (1242), Sivas, Kayseri, Erzincan and Ankara

wars.outcome: The Mongols under Baiju took Erzurum in 1242 and crushed Kaykhusraw II on 26 June 1243; Rum became a client kingdom paying tribute.

wars.name: Battle of Aksaray
wars.outcome: Bayju defeated Kaykaus II on 14 October 1256 and 'all of Anatolia became officially subject to Möngke Khan'.

wars.name: Battle of Elbistan and the Karamanid capture of Konya
wars.outcome: After Baibars beat the Mongols at Elbistan the Karamanids captured Konya and installed a puppet, Jimri, briefly.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given by any page; the frontiers with the Byzantines, the beyliks and the Armenian and Ayyubid lands are approximate throughout, and from 1243 the sultanate's extent is blurred by Mongol administration.

notes: Page budget 9 of 9 used. Unsettled: (1) Cliopatria's 1094-1098 shape (367,020 km2, with Nicaea, Smyrna, Antalya, Kastamonu) is only verified for Nicaea and the western cities lost in 1097; the extent in 1077-1093 and the 1086-1092 interregnum is a bridge. (2) The Abbasid-allegiance relation (1202-1249) is Cliopatria's; no page opened mentions the caliph (the Rum and Kayqubad I pages are silent), so no vassal event was written; open 'Al-Nasir' or 'Abbasid Caliphate'. (3) Gains of 1188 (Kayseri and the west to Dorylaeum/Afyon) and 1202 (Kastamonu, bbox 27.6 E) are not dated by any page: confidence 1 or unverified. (4) 1260-1304 has no Cliopatria shape; the dossier keeps Rum alive as an Ilkhanid vassal and draws the 1305 core; the Mongol Empire and Ilkhanate dossiers (ia-02) should record vassal_start for Rum in 1243 (Köse Dağ) and 1256 (Aksaray) and decide whether the vassal tint applies to the Rum land. (5) The Mamluk 1260s-1270s Cilician and Elbistan frontiers, and the Karamanid capture of Konya (1277) are given as contests only. (6) Counterparts needing dossiers: saltukids (Erzurum), the Seljuk emirate of Erzurum (Tughril 1192-1221, Jahan Shah to 1230), mengujekids (Erzincan, Divriği), artuqids. (7) The Kayqubad I page's claims of Siverek, Urfa, Harran and Raqqa in 1234 are very likely raids; the ayyubid-sultanate dossier (me-09) should say whether those cities changed hands. (8) Kaykaus I's Aleppo episode of 1216-1218 is a vassal-alliance with al-Afdal, not territory. (9) The Third Crusade occupation of Konya (1190) is recorded as a one-year contest with the Holy Roman Empire. (10) Gazetteer names needed: Alanya, Ahlat, Siverek, Philadelphia (Alaşehir), Choma (Honaz): coordinates used.
